walkthroughs.body_html:
Resource Security — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Resource Security brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Resource Security.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the Hubbert curve about?
options: Peak oil
Population
Climate
Migration
Africa
South America
Australia
Central Asia

mcqs.q: What is the difference between physical and economic water scarcity?
options: HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.
Water scarcity only happens in dry countries.

Physical scarcity is insufficient water supply for demand (e.g. arid regions); economic scarcity is inability to access available water due to lack of infrastructure or investment, despite water being present.

mcqs.q: What are the four pillars of food security?
options: Food security just means producing enough food.
HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.
Availability (enough food exists), access (people can obtain it), utilisation (nutritional quality and absorption) and stability (consistent over time) — defined by the FAO.
Food security means storing food for emergencies.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes typically cause more deaths in LICs than HICs?
options: HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.
LICs often have poorly enforced building codes, weak emergency response, dense informal housing and limited preparedness — not because the earthquakes are stronger.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.
LICs have more earthquake deaths because more earthquakes happen there.
